react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of ten differentially abundant metabolites reveals robust perturbation of sterol and cholesterol-associated pathways as the dominant biological signal. Cholesterol (KEGG:C00187, ChEBI:16113) is the single most-connected node: it achieves fold-enrichment of 6755 in RaMP ORA for intestinal lipid absorption (REACT:R-HSA-8963678, FDR=0.0027), appears as the sole member hit in the KEGG steroid-biosynthesis pathway (hsa00100, p=0.099), and dominates the mummichog m/z-direct ranking with significant hits in bile-acid biosynthesis (p=0.021), C21-steroid-hormone biosynthesis (p=0.021), squalene and cholesterol biosynthesis (p=0.048), and glycerophospholipid metabolism (p=0.033). InChIKey reconciliation confirmed cholesterol's structure (HVYWMOMLDIMFJA-DPAQBDIFSA-N) with no namespace artefacts. The second-strongest driver is 4-pyridoxic acid (KEGG:C00847, ChEBI:17405), which is the top-ranked MetaboAnalystR KEGG hit (vitamin B6 metabolism, hsa00750, p=0.0224) and corroborates in RaMP (metabolism of vitamins and cofactors, REACT:R-HSA-196854, FDR=0.0027) and mummichog (vitamin B6 pyridoxine metabolism, p=0.033). Uric acid (KEGG:C00366, ChEBI:17775) independently supports purine metabolism across RaMP and MetaboAnalystR, while coumarin (KEGG:C05851, ChEBI:28794) drives Phase I xenobiotic functionalisation and biological oxidations hits in RaMP (FDR=0.0027). The convergence of a major cholesterol-centered sterol axis with perturbed vitamin B6 catabolism and secondary purine/xenobiotic signals suggests a treatment-associated metabolic shift affecting lipid absorption, cofactor homeostasis, and oxidative xenobiotic metabolism.

Both mummichog (MUMM:squalene_and_cholesterol_biosynthesis, rank 9) and MetaboAnalystR (KEGG:hsa00100 Steroid biosynthesis, rank 1) converge on a cholesterol-centric sterol axis. react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of ten differentially abundant metabolites identified cholesterol as the dominant signal. In the mummichog m/z-direct paradigm, MUMM:bile_acid_biosynthesis ranked first (p=0.018) with cholesterol as the sole input hit; in the RaMP ORA paradigm, REACT:R-HSA-1430728 Metabolism ranked first (FDR=0.000134) with cholesterol among a four-metabolite hit set. Both mummichog (MUMM:squalene_and_cholesterol_biosynthesis, rank 9) and MetaboAnalystR (KEGG:hsa00100 Steroid biosynthesis, rank 1) converge on a cholesterol-centric sterol axis. Cholesterol is a direct member of REACT:R-HSA-8963678 Intestinal lipid absorption (FDR=0.00271, fold-enrichment=6755.1) in RaMP ORA, confirming the sterol axis extends to lipid-handling processes. 4-Pyridoxic acid is the driver of the vitamin B6 catabolism signal: it is a member of MUMM:vitamin_b6_pyridoxine_metabolism (rank 5, p=0.031) in mummichog and the sole input hit of KEGG:hsa00750 Vitamin B6 metabolism (rank 0, p=0.022) in MetaboAnalystR. Uric acid is the driver of purine-related perturbations: it appears as the sole input hit of REACT:R-HSA-5619071 Defective SLC22A12 causes renal hypouricemia 1 in RaMP ORA and is a member of KEGG:hsa00230 Purine metabolism (rank 3, p=0.165) in MetaboAnalystR. Coumarin is the driver of xenobiotic perturbation: it is a direct member of MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism (rank 3, p=0.031) in mummichog and of REACT:R-HSA-211945 Phase I - Functionalization of compounds (FDR=0.00266) and REACT:R-HSA-211859 Biological oxidations (FDR=0.00271) in RaMP ORA. A convergence of the cholesterol-centered sterol axis with perturbed vitamin B6 catabolism, secondary purine signals, and xenobiotic functionalisation is observed across ORA, m/z-direct, and KEGG-specific paradigms.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm pathway analysis of ten differentially abundant metabolites identified cholesterol as the dominant signal. In the mummichog m/z-direct paradigm, MUMM:bile_acid_biosynthesis ranked first (p=0.018) with cholesterol as the sole input hit; in the RaMP ORA paradigm, REACT:R-HSA-1430728 Metabolism ranked first (FDR=0.000134) with cholesterol among a four-metabolite hit set. Both mummichog (MUMM:squalene_and_cholesterol_biosynthesis, rank 9) and MetaboAnalystR (KEGG:hsa00100 Steroid biosynthesis, rank 1) converge on a cholesterol-centric sterol axis. Cholesterol is a direct member of REACT:R-HSA-8963678 Intestinal lipid absorption (FDR=0.00271, fold-enrichment=6755.1) in RaMP ORA, confirming the sterol axis extends to lipid-handling processes. 4-Pyridoxic acid is the driver of the vitamin B6 catabolism signal: it is a member of MUMM:vitamin_b6_pyridoxine_metabolism (rank 5, p=0.031) in mummichog and the sole input hit of KEGG:hsa00750 Vitamin B6 metabolism (rank 0, p=0.022) in MetaboAnalystR. Uric acid is the driver of purine-related perturbations: it appears as the sole input hit of REACT:R-HSA-5619071 Defective SLC22A12 causes renal hypouricemia 1 in RaMP ORA and is a member of KEGG:hsa00230 Purine metabolism (rank 3, p=0.165) in MetaboAnalystR. Coumarin is the driver of xenobiotic perturbation: it is a direct member of MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism (rank 3, p=0.031) in mummichog and of REACT:R-HSA-211945 Phase I - Functionalization of compounds (FDR=0.00266) and REACT:R-HSA-211859 Biological oxidations (FDR=0.00271) in RaMP ORA. A convergence of the cholesterol-centered sterol axis with perturbed vitamin B6 catabolism, secondary purine signals, and xenobiotic functionalisation is observed across ORA, m/z-direct, and KEGG-specific paradigms.
